items.title: The Clock Is Ticking on These 4 Dividend Stocks and Deadlines Are Just Days Away
items.summary: Four dividend deadlines are converging this week, and missing the cutoff by even one trading session pushes the next payment a full quarter away. Before you buy, there are a few balance sheet details on these names worth checking first.

items.title: Prediction: This Out-of-Favor Dividend Stock Could Have Significant Upside
items.summary: PepsiCo sits near a 52-week low while the rest of the market chases AI momentum, and the gap between where it trades and where the fundamentals point is getting harder to ignore.

items.title: 2 Large-Cap Stocks with Solid Fundamentals and 1 We Brush Off
items.summary: Large-cap stocks usually command their industries because they have the scale to drive market trends. The flip side though is that their sheer size can limit growth as expanding further becomes an increasingly challenging task.

items.title: This Warren Buffett Favorite Still Has Room to Run
items.summary: Warren Buffett has held Coca-Cola since 1988, and after a 35% run over the past year, most investors assume the opportunity has passed. Our model disagrees, and the reason comes down to one number buried inside the latest earnings report.

items.title: Pepsi’s Fall Continues: One Prominent Firm’s Resolute Target Implies 41% Gains Moving Forward
items.summary: PepsiCo has shed nearly 7% this year while the S&P 500 climbed double digits, yet one prominent firm refuses to abandon a price target that towers far above Wall Street consensus and hinges on a very specific set of dominoes falling into place.

items.title: Should You Buy PepsiCo Stock Because Its International Business Keeps Accelerating?
items.summary: PepsiCo (PEP) stock traded at $129.75 on September 18, the lowest price of its past 52 weeks. The worry is North America, where sales of snacks and drinks have disappointed. Yet the part of PepsiCo that sells outside the U.S. is growing faster and earning more on each sale. The share price appears to give that part little credit.

items.title: PepsiCo Falls 3% While Consumer Staples Hold Firm; Keurig Dr. Pepper Eases, Coca-Cola Barely Budges
items.summary: PepsiCo is sliding hard on Friday while Coca-Cola sits nearly flat and the broader consumer staples sector barely flinches, and that split raises a pointed question about what exactly the market is punishing.
